review.rationale: Initial release budgets replace the debug-only 120/180 second launch ceilings. Absolute limits are safety rails calibrated from local release observations and the first same-host GitHub runner release comparison, while the current-main comparison remains the primary 20 percent regression gate.

evidence.source: Issue #49: 2026-08-25 Linux WebKit measurements and implementation baseline runs
PR #58 run 32942547888: Linux AppImage baseline/candidate startup p95 was 31.40/31.47 seconds on the same hosted runner with at most 0.69 percent difference

PR #58 runs 32942547888, 32946504534, and 32950388617: identical bootstrap catalog hooks kept refresh p50 within 785.39-813.42 ms while first-browser p95 ranged from 873.86-1727.80 ms; cached-read p95 ranged from 3.17-59.56 ms

PR #58 runs 32946504534, 32950388617, and 32953791298: identical Windows bootstrap sources kept candidate warm-start p50 changes to 16.0, 1.9, and 8.6 percent; run 32953791298 failed p95 only because one 984.97 ms Tukey outlier exceeded the 765.82 ms baseline p95

PR #124 run 33912788179: an unrelated Marketplace launch-retry change produced a 2048.374 ms Windows cold-start p95 against a 1472.412 ms baseline (575.962 ms absolute difference) while the installed MSI and NSIS performance suites passed
Main runs 33919703993 and 33925549585: Linux release navigation p95 missed its relative gate by 3.441 ms and 21.326 ms respectively on unrelated test-only changes

Issue #176 runs 35697751425 and 35703788546: unpacking the AppImage once and requesting pageLoadStrategy none both left Linux cold/warm startup near 32 seconds; launch-stage instrumentation isolated 17.9-32.4 seconds inside hosted WebKitWebDriver POST /session while the explicit shell wait took 0.5-1.1 seconds

Issue #176 run 35710680908: keying both variants' binary caches on a build-input fingerprint cut the candidate legs from 222-312 s to 12-28 s and the Release performance wall clock from 978 s to 481 s with every gate green and no change to matrix dimensions, sample counts, or the 300-second idle windows

coldStartupMs.rationale: Hosted Linux custom-binary WebKitWebDriver spends 17.9 to 32.4 seconds inside POST /session before the explicit application-shell wait, while AppImage extraction mode and the standard pageLoadStrategy capability do not change the plateau. The workflow now supplies the desktop session bus expected by WebKitGTK and keeps launch-stage timing visible. The 40 second absolute rail remains unchanged until corrected hosted evidence is reviewed; the same-host 20 percent comparison is the working regression gate.

warmStartupMs.rationale: Warm startup shares the same hosted WebKitWebDriver POST /session plateau as cold startup even though the following explicit shell wait is only 0.5 to 1.1 seconds. The workflow supplies a desktop session bus without changing the ready-shell condition, sample count, or cache semantics. The unchanged 40 second safety rail will be tightened only after corrected hosted evidence is available.

firstIpcMs.rationale: The environment IPC observation was 346 ms; this retains hosted-runner headroom.

environmentSlowMs.rationale: A tracked 400 ms backend delay verifies that slow environment discovery remains observable and bounded.

environmentTimeoutRecoveryMs.rationale: A client deadline against a two-second probe must recover on the next normal environment request. The 6000 ms absolute rail still reads p95, but the relative comparison reads p50 because the p95 of this metric is not a distribution tail. Across twenty-six Linux sample sets the second of the three post-warm-up samples was the maximum in twenty-two of them, so nearest-rank p95 at n=3 re-measures one reproducible blip whose size swings between 1.05 and 2.36 times the median. Comparing two draws of that blip failed three of thirteen product-unchanged runs; comparing medians failed one.

catalogCachedMs.rationale: A valid disk catalog must be visible without waiting for an isolated refresh. Three same-host bootstrap comparisons observed 3.17-59.56 ms p95, so this metric uses a reviewed 75 ms floor while retaining the 750 ms safety ceiling.

catalogRefreshMs.rationale: The isolated loopback catalog fixture remains independent of external Marketplace health and gates p50 because browser bootstrap makes p95 unstable. Seventeen product-unchanged comparisons put p50 between 706 and 1331 ms and the same-run absolute delta between 29 and 362 ms; the 20 percent allowance failed once when a low 944 ms baseline reduced it below the observed additive noise. A reviewed 400 ms floor covers that corpus with 38 ms headroom. To compensate rather than relax quality, the absolute p50 rail is tightened from 15000 to 4000 ms, still 3.0 times the largest observed p50.

smallWorkspaceScanMs.rationale: The one-project observation was 16 ms and should not regress into user-visible delay.

largeWorkspaceScanMs.rationale: The realistic tier carries enough projects and bytes to expose linear scan regressions, and the 12000 ms rail still reads p95 for that. The relative comparison reads p50 because this metric's p95 at n=3 is one sporadic blip, not a tail. Across thirty-two Linux sample sets p50 stayed within 18.0 to 44.4 ms and the candidate-to-baseline p50 gap never exceeded 14.2 ms, while p95 ranged from 21.0 to 143.0 ms and reached three to four times the median in six of them. The maximum lands at index 0, 1, or 2 in five, sixteen, and eleven sets, so unlike environmentTimeoutRecoveryMs and navigationMs this blip is not positional; the relative gate was subtracting two independent draws of it and read -57.89 to +107.75 percent on product-unchanged runs, failing one of sixteen. Medians failed none, the 50 ms floor still catches a sustained 35 ms shift against the observed 14.2 ms gap, and the largest value ever seen on the rail is 143 ms.

navigationMs.rationale: Observed debug navigation was 111 to 248 ms. Hosted Linux release comparisons can jitter by tens of milliseconds on unrelated changes, so navigation uses a reviewed 100 ms floor while retaining its 20 percent and 1.5 second gates. The rail still reads p95, but the relative comparison reads p50 because the three samples are three different routes rather than three draws of one workload: the harness walks Projects, Settings, and Studio Pro once each. Across thirty-eight Linux sample sets the per-index means were 100.8, 145.7, and 42.0 ms and the maximum fell on Settings in thirty-five, so nearest-rank p95 at n=3 compared a single sample of the most expensive route. The one relative failure in nineteen product-unchanged runs read 117/133/59 against 76/267/68, where the median improved from 117 to 76 ms; p50 failed none. Relative coverage stays at one route and moves from Settings to the middle route, so a Settings-only regression now reaches only the rail.

coldStartupMs.rationale: Installed package launch must create its native window within a user-visible budget.

warmStartupMs.rationale: Repeated installed package launches exercise the warmed OS and WebView caches.

idleCpuPercent.rationale: Installed package idle CPU uses the same normalized process-tree meaning.

privateMemoryBytes.rationale: Installed package private memory uses the release WebView safety ceiling.

workingSetBytes.rationale: Installed package RSS is reported separately from private memory.

processCount.rationale: Installed package root and live descendants use the same bounded process-tree scope.

privateMemoryGrowthBytes.rationale: Installed package private-memory growth is bounded across the five-minute window.

workingSetGrowthBytes.rationale: Installed package working-set growth is tracked separately from private bytes.

processCountGrowth.rationale: Installed package child-process growth is checked across the full idle window.

coldStartupMs.rationale: Release WebView2 startup replaces the former 180 second CI override with a 20 second safety rail. Hosted-runner cold p95 can vary by roughly 0.6 seconds for unrelated changes, so a metric-specific 600 ms floor avoids false positives while retaining the 20 percent and 20 second gates.

warmStartupMs.rationale: Warm release startup excludes Rust compilation and Vite readiness. Across three same-host bootstrap comparisons, candidate p50 changes stayed within 16 percent while a single 984.97 ms Tukey outlier produced a 28.62 percent p95 false positive; p95 remains reported and the relative gate uses p50.

firstIpcMs.rationale: Native environment discovery gets explicit hosted Windows variance headroom.

environmentSlowMs.rationale: A tracked 400 ms backend delay verifies that slow native discovery stays observable and bounded.

environmentTimeoutRecoveryMs.rationale: WebView2 must recover after a client deadline without requiring an application restart.

catalogCachedMs.rationale: Cached Marketplace state must render without a live browser refresh.

catalogRefreshMs.rationale: The isolated browser fixture has its own ceiling and never depends on live Marketplace health. Across seventeen product-unchanged comparisons the Windows samples were bimodal: fast 1410-4919 ms and slow 6492-21997 ms, with the baseline first sample in the slow mode in every run but only two of fifty-one candidate samples slow. At three samples nearest-rank p95 is the maximum, so the relative gate compares bootstrap modes rather than product latency. A reviewed 4500 ms floor covers all seventeen same-code comparisons while the unchanged 20000 ms absolute p95 rail still bounds the measured tail.

smallWorkspaceScanMs.rationale: Small native workspace discovery should remain well below the old 10 second ceiling.

largeWorkspaceScanMs.rationale: The large tier bounds registry and filesystem scanning on hosted Windows.

navigationMs.rationale: WebView2 navigation should stay interactive under hosted runner noise.

coldStartupMs.rationale: Installed MSI and NSIS cold launches must create a native window within 20 seconds.

warmStartupMs.rationale: Warm installer launches isolate application startup from installation time.

idleCpuPercent.rationale: Installed WebView2 process-tree CPU uses five-minute normalized sampling.

privateMemoryBytes.rationale: MSI and NSIS package memory shares the release WebView2 safety ceiling.

workingSetBytes.rationale: Installed bundle RSS remains independently visible and bounded.

processCount.rationale: Installed Tauri and WebView2 root and descendants are counted at every sample.

privateMemoryGrowthBytes.rationale: Installed bundle private-memory growth is bounded across the five-minute window.

workingSetGrowthBytes.rationale: Installed bundle working-set growth is tracked separately from private bytes.

processCountGrowth.rationale: The installed process tree may not leak descendants during five minutes idle.
